gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the RYOBI MICROTECH FVD02K, which ChatGPT offered as the ~$50 alternative, publishes only one powered torque figure, 'up to .2 Nm' (1.77 in-lb). That is 4× the 0.05 N·m (0.44 in-lb) low step on the Fanttik E1 MAX and E2 Ultra. The iFixit driver's single 0.15 N·m (1.33 in-lb) is 3×. The 'manual torque' figures (3 N·m on the E1 MAX, 1.0 N·m on the iFixit) are hand-applied limits 15× and 6.7× the motor cap, so they don't belong in a headline torque comparison.
standout_why: Pages compared: Fanttik's 'HOTO vs Fanttik' blog (cited by ChatGPT in every chat) gives the E1 MAX, E2 Ultra and S2 Pro settings in N·m only. It has no HOTO figures, no manual-mode torque and nothing on RYOBI or iFixit. Fanttik's 'E1 vs E2' blog lists 'Power / manual' as a mode but gives no manual torque value. toolengineers.com (rank 1 in every chat) gives values only for the E1 MAX ('around 0.05 and 0.2 N·m') and leaves the HOTO, Wowstick and Miniware torque fields blank. It doesn't mention RYOBI, Hyper Tough or iFixit. butactuallygood.com calls the E1 MAX 'apparently fixed' at 0.2 N·m, which Fanttik's own support page contradicts with a 0.05 N·m low step. It lists a 'HOTO 25-Piece Kit' at '4' N·m, and doesn't mention RYOBI or iFixit. None of these pages converts to in-lb, separates motor torque from manual torque across brands, or points out that two of the cheaper alternatives ChatGPT surfaced publish no torque below 0.15 to 0.2 N·m. The E1 MAX's 0.05/0.2 values are already in the cited Fanttik pages, so the new part is the cross-brand floor comparison and the manual-torque footnote. That's why this is a 2, not a 3.
decides: It supports the Fanttik E1 MAX or E2 Ultra over the RYOBI MICROTECH and the iFixit driver for phone, watch and camera screws. On maker figures, only the Fanttiks offer a powered step below 0.15 N·m: 0.05 N·m, a quarter of the RYOBI's only published figure. RYOBI's '2 speeds' and '2 Modes' come with no lower torque number, so for delicate work the shopper can't assume one exists. The iFixit's 0.15 N·m fixed cap at $22.95 still works as a budget pick for laptop and console screws. The E2 Ultra's 0.6 N·m top step (5.31 in-lb) is the only powered figure here above 0.2 N·m. That supports ChatGPT's 'E2 Ultra for mixed PC work' line. Manual torque (E1 MAX 3 N·m vs iFixit 1.0 N·m) only matters for breaking loose stuck screws, not for strip-safety.
